He wouldn't move. So China built the road around his house.
Wenling, 2012. Duck farmer Luo Baogen has just built a five-storey home.
Then the city plans a new road. Straight through it.
Four hundred homes are in the way. Everyone takes the money.
They offer two hundred and sixty thousand. He says no.
So the road gets built anyway. Around him.
He and his wife sleep on different floors, so nobody can knock down half.
China has a name for this: a nail house.
And he wasn't the first. Chongqing, 2007: one stood on a pillar of dirt, in the middle of a construction pit.
Photos of Luo's house go around the world.
About a week later, he signs. He moves out, and the diggers move in.
